summary: Service account IAM role changes not applied after Okta group membership update — CI artifact pulls fail
description:
Issue summary:
After an Okta group update (ci-service-accounts -> added build-runner-main@svc.redwood) the corresponding IAM role change did not appear in Redwood's internal IAM service. Result: nightly CI batch jobs failed to pull artifacts from internal artifact-registry with 403 Forbidden for the affected service account.

Impact:
- Multiple CI pipelines in prod-us-east failed for ~3 hours (build-runner-main service account).
- Customer-facing deployments blocked for a small subset of push events (~10% of nightly runs).
- Operational exposure for Dedicated customers running on the same pipelines.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (Okta org: redwood-prod)
- Identity sync path: Okta SCIM -> identity-service (k8s) -> IAM role-mapper -> artifact-registry ACLs

Observed behavior:
- Okta audit shows group membership change at 2026-03-10T02:11:04Z.
- SCIM webhook delivery logs show 200 OK to identity-service endpoint.
- identity-service processed event but role-mapper logged an error and did not apply the new role.
- artifact-registry returned 403 for token attempts by service account.

Priority rationale: P1 due to production CI blockage affecting deployments and customer SLAs.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) In Okta (prod org) add service account 'build-runner-main@svc.redwood' to group 'ci-service-accounts'.
2) Observe SCIM webhook delivery in Okta admin -> System logs.
3) Check identity-service /metrics and logs for processing of the SCIM event.
4) Attempt artifact pull via runner using the service account credentials and observe 403 if role not propagated.
logs:
identity-service ERROR role-mapper: failed to map group 'ci-service-accounts' -> mapping not found (config-id: maps/roles.yaml) at 2026-03-10T02:11:05Z
artifact-registry auth denied token for subject build-runner-main@svc.redwood: missing 'artifact:pull' role at 2026-03-10T02:12:02Z
okta-webhook INFO delivered event Id=evt_9a3f at 2026-03-10T02:11:04Z status=200
scheduler WARN backfill-job-queue: task retry threshold reached for service-account build-runner-main at 2026-03-10T03:45:00Z
comments: Aisha Khatri (reporter) 2026-03-10: Noticed multiple nightly CI failures after adding service account to ci-service-accounts in Okta. Created this ticket to track sync failure.

Noah Patel (assignee) 2026-03-10: Investigating identity-service logs. Initial hypothesis: role-mapper config mismatch or recently deployed mapping change on 2026-03-09. Pulling audit logs and config history.
SRE-Team (via #internal-auth) 2026-03-10: Observed same symptom for a second service account. Shared temporary workaround: manually grant 'artifact:pull' via IAM console to unblock CI.

Noah Patel 2026-03-11: Found failing mapping rule in maps/roles.yaml introduced by PR 4256 (renamed group label from 'ci-service-accounts' to 'ci-runners'). identity-service expects the old key; SCIM events still reference the old group name. Drafting hotfix PR to add fallback mapping.
Security (review) 2026-03-11: Confirmed manual grant is a minimal privilege temporary fix. Requesting audit of backfilled grants and notification to security team post-mitigation.

Noah Patel 2026-03-12: Merged PR 4321 to add fallback mapping and a safety check; re-ran backfill script to reconcile 14 service accounts. CI pipelines green as of 2026-03-12T09:04:00Z. Closing after monitoring window.
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-10T02:11:04Z: Okta group change event visible in Okta audit.
- 2026-03-10T02:11:05Z: identity-service accepted webhook but role-mapper returned error mapping lookup failed.
- 2026-03-10T02:12:00Z - 03:45:00Z: CI jobs repeatedly failed with 403.
Findings:
- A configuration change (PR 4256) two days earlier renamed keys in maps/roles.yaml but did not include compatibility aliases. SCIM events still reference the canonical group string.
- identity-service did not have a fallback for unknown group keys and logged the failure without retrying with alias resolution.
- The scheduler/backfill feature had an intermittent crash and did not apply pending reconciliation jobs; restarted the job controller to flush backlog.
Actions taken:
- Applied temporary IAM grants to unblock critical runners.
- Hotfix PR 4321 added alias support and an automated alert if mapping lookup fails more than 3x for the same subject.
- Backfill script re-run to reconcile all affected service accounts.
- Added unit tests and a small integration test for SCIM->role-mapper mappings.
resolution:
Root cause: role-mapping key change in maps/roles.yaml (PR 4256) created a mismatch with Okta group keys; identity-service had no alias/fallback path and the backfill controller experienced a separate restart that delayed reconciliation.
Fix: Merged PR 4321 to add alias lookup and failure alerting, re-ran backfill (reconciled 14 accounts), and applied temporary manual grants for immediate unblocking.
Follow-ups: 1) Add a CI gate that flags role-mapping changes without compatibility aliases (owner: identity). 2) Enhance monitoring for mapping lookup failures (owner: SRE). 3) Add a runbook entry to Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ID/pages/44122/okta-scim-sync-runbook.
Status: Resolved and verified (CI passing, no further 403s as of 2026-03-12T09:30:00Z).
